name: Anti-environmentalism
summary: Anti-environmentalism opposes environmentalism or specific environmental policies, mostly on grounds of property rights, limited government, and economic growth. It holds that markets, technology and prosperity protect the environment better than regulation, that climate and conservation rules cost more than they deliver, and that rural resource users and national sovereignty are overridden by distant bureaucracies and international agreements.
scope: The mainstream English-language, mostly American, countermovement: the 1980s wise use movement (Ron Arnold, Alan Gottlieb), free-market environmentalism and think tanks such as Cato and Heritage, cost-benefit skepticism of Bjorn Lomborg, Julian Simon-style cornucopianism, and 'response skepticism' toward climate policy as in President Trump's 2017 Paris withdrawal. Excludes outright climate-science denial as a defining position, and European far-right strands beyond what the sources note.

keyFigures.name: Ron Arnold
keyFigures.role: Wise use movement organiser who urged defeating environmentalism and wrote Ecology Wars.

keyFigures.name: Bjørn Lomborg
keyFigures.role: Author of The Skeptical Environmentalist, arguing environmental trends and policy costs are misjudged.

keyFigures.name: Julian Simon
keyFigures.role: Economist whose The Ultimate Resource argued population and ingenuity overcome resource scarcity.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Healthcare is outside the movement's concerns; its limited-government, anti-bureaucracy stance and think-tank base (Cato, Heritage) point to a market-based rather than state-guaranteed system.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not an environmental issue; the pro-business, anti-intervention outlook of its industry and think-tank backers implies opposition to wage mandates.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Free-market environmentalism holds that prices, property rights and tort law protect resources better than regulators, and Cato and Heritage favor competitive markets over public approaches.

public-ownership.rationale: Wise use opposes federal control of land and resources and favors private and local use; public ownership of energy is contrary to its approach.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from its small-government, pro-business backing; the sources do not address taxes on the wealthy.

unions-good.rationale: Wise use courted resource workers (loggers, miners) as allies, but the movement's industry funders and free-enterprise outlook are often hostile to unions; adherents are split.

property-fundamental.rationale: Wise use ties the right to use natural resources to life, liberty and property, and presses against regulatory limits on owners.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Opposition to environmental regulation of industry and to a large bureaucracy is the movement's defining position.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; limited-government adherents lean to cuts but the movement's rural, resource-community base is often welfare-dependent.

worker-ownership.rationale: Its property-rights framework favors private owners; collective worker ownership is not part of it and is inferred as disfavored.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No documented position; libertarian strands oppose, security-minded conservative strands support.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; libertarian-leaning members favor, conservatives oppose.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's liberty rhetoric and conservative base suggest opposition to speech restrictions.

strong-leader.rationale: Inferred from its distrust of concentrated government power and its emphasis on individual freedom.

state-harmful.rationale: It wants a limited, non-interventionist state and sees public environmental management as authoritarian, but it does not call for abolishing the state, and several strands want the state to protect property and open land to development.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the western rural, property-rights and individual-liberty culture of wise use; no source addresses guns directly.

empower-police-military.rationale: The sources record no stance on police and military funding; the conservative base leans supportive while the libertarian base is wary of state power.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Sex work is untouched by the movement, and its libertarian and religious-conservative strands pull in opposite directions.

decide-locally.rationale: Wise use wants control moved from federal agencies to local communities and rural residents; it argues national forests were meant to serve nearby communities.

rehabilitation.rationale: Prison policy is untouched in the sources, and nothing in property-rights or anti-regulation thinking settles it.

traditional-family.rationale: A study cited in the Wikipedia article links opposition to environmentalism on the American right to defending Christian values, family and traditional masculinity.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the conservative cultural alignment noted in studies of the American right, though libertarian strands disagree.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the conservative cultural alignment, with libertarian dissent.

more-religion-public.rationale: Critics claim fundamentalist beliefs influence the movement; the sources show a religious-conservative strand but not a program.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the conservative, anti-intervention outlook.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the cultural conservatism noted in studies of the American right.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The American-right study links the stance to defending traditions; rural-community heritage is a wise use theme.

gradual-change.rationale: Not addressed; adherents defend existing uses against change, but also demand radical rollback of regulation.

reduce-immigration.rationale: European far-right anti-climate parties favor it, whereas business-oriented adherents favor immigration; split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Opposition to international climate agreements as infringing sovereignty is explicit: the Paris withdrawal was framed as a reassertion of sovereignty.

free-trade.rationale: Industry adherents favor open markets, yet the Paris statement is framed around national economic advantage and stricter burden-sharing; adherents are split.

nation-first.rationale: Trump framed withdrawal from Paris as putting US workers and sovereignty first and said the accord disadvantages the US; this reflects a mainstream national-interest strand.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: No source links the movement to foreign intervention; its sovereignty focus points against, while hawkish conservative backers point for.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; European far-right strands oppose and nothing in the sources supports open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Lomborg and Simon-style cornucopians hold that growth and wealth reduce pollution and solve environmental problems, and that development should precede environmental spending.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Opponents reject drastic action: the Paris statement cites job losses and trivial temperature effect, and Lomborg holds Kyoto costs more than it delivers.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Lomborg expects technological improvement to meet energy needs, and Julian Simon-style cornucopianism holds that ingenuity overcomes shortages; Arnold likewise argues technology addresses environmental problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The movement favors an open competitive energy market and more energy production; nuclear is rarely discussed so this is inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Inferred; the movement works through lobbying, litigation and electoral politics, though some militia-adjacent strands differ.

experts-over-public.rationale: It disputes scientific environmental establishment claims and favors local, rural views over agency expertise.

central-planning.rationale: Free-market environmentalism argues regulation creates a political commons and that markets and property rights outperform planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred from its private-property emphasis; not addressed directly.

land-value-tax.rationale: Some free-market environmentalists (geolibertarians) support it, but it is not a wise use position.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from its pro-property, pro-business orientation.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from limited-government view.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trump-style nationalism favors tariffs, market-liberal think tanks oppose; split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Cato and Heritage favor private incentives over public approaches in energy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Wise use rhetoric centers on individuals, ranchers and small resource users, but this is not a stated program.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary policy is outside the sources; free-market libertarians would agree while mainstream think tanks would not.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to state-directed economic bodies inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Rejected by its liberty and limited-government framing.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Forms of head of state are irrelevant to the movement, which operates in republican and parliamentary democracies.

democracy-best.rationale: Wise use works through democratic and legal channels and claims rural voices are ignored; no source states a view on democracy as such.

direct-votes.rationale: Wise use favors local control, but the sources show no position on referendums versus representation.

workers-councils.rationale: Incompatible with its private-property, free-enterprise orientation.

right-to-secede.rationale: Some western property-rights activists favor state-level control of federal land, but secession is not a movement position.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from individualist outlook.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between mainstream lobbying and fringe rhetoric.

war-builds-character.rationale: No source touches it; the movement's commercial, growth-and-jobs framing makes glorifying war unlikely.

separate-church-state.rationale: Adherents divided between libertarian and religious-conservative strands.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: A religious-conservative strand exists, but scripture-based law is not a movement position.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Tort law and private enforcement matter to free-market environmentalism, but private defense is not a position.

military-superiority.rationale: Defense posture is not in the sources; nationalist strands favor it while the cost-conscious limited-government strand is lukewarm.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Not addressed; far-right European strands may differ but the mainstream does not hold it.

class-struggle-history.rationale: A free-enterprise position rejects class conflict as the driver of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Free-market environmentalism relies on prices and property incentives, which are incompatible with an aim of equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Wise use seeks private and local resource use over restrictions; indigenous authority over land conflicts with its development agenda.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Its objection to Paris-style transfers such as the Green Climate Fund suggests opposition to reparations by analogy.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from sovereignty emphasis.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Free-market environmentalism relies on owners' self-interest and incentives rather than moral appeals.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Wise use frames resource use as an individual right, not a duty to the community.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Arnold characterizes environmentalism as anti-humanity; opponents stress human uses, though some adherents value nature instrumentally for recreation.

limit-population.rationale: Cornucopians such as Simon see population as an asset, not a problem, and Lomborg rejects Malthusian predictions.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Lomborg documents rising prosperity, life expectancy and food supply as industrial gains.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Cornucopian faith in technology and growth supports it, though the movement defends existing industries rather than disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Technological optimism favors enhancement, while the religious-conservative strand is wary; no source speaks to it.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from distrust of bureaucracy.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption is outside the sources; libertarian strands favor it and security-minded conservatives do not.

restore-past-order.rationale: Defends traditional rural land use, but also rests on progress and growth; split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Lomborg uses cost-benefit analysis, but the movement is strongly ideological about property.

direct-action.rationale: It organizes mainly through lobbying and litigation.

means-match-ends.rationale: The movement has no stated view on whether methods must mirror aims; it is pragmatic lobbying and litigation.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Lomborg's progress narrative and Simon-style abundance reject this.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Property rights and price signals, not need, allocate goods in the free-market framework it adopts.

production-for-use.rationale: The movement defends profit-making enterprise and market incentives as the way to produce and conserve resources.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Profit and enterprise are defended as beneficial.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A free-enterprise, limited-government movement is fundamentally opposed to dictatorship of any class.

collective-farming.rationale: The wise use constituency is individual ranchers, farmers and landowners defending private use against collective control.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Opposed to the premise of the capitalist critique.

taxation-theft.rationale: Libertarian free-market strands hold it, but the mainstream (Cato, Heritage, politicians such as Trump) accepts taxation; split.

harm-principle.rationale: Wise use rejects many harm-based environmental restrictions but does not state this principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Wise use stresses individual rights, but also community and group claims such as rural community traditions.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberty emphasis.

exit-over-voice.rationale: No source addresses it; rural communities complain of lacking voice, but the movement does not rank exit above voting.

state-as-business.rationale: Market-friendly think tanks sympathize with business-like government, but citizens-as-customers is not a stated position.

positive-liberty.rationale: It treats freedom as non-interference and property use; rejects state provision as authoritarian.

media-academia-power.rationale: The movement and Wikipedia article note perceived bias in media and science establishment against rural and industry views.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Race and ability are not part of the movement's concerns; the mainstream is unlikely to endorse it.

organic-representation.rationale: It works through parties, lobbying and courts, not corporatist representation by bodies.

total-state.rationale: It opposes large bureaucracy and views public environmental management as authoritarian.

national-rebirth.rationale: Nostalgic rural themes exist, but radical national renewal is not stated by wise use or free-market sources.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Its nationalism is inward, framed as sovereignty and economic advantage, not expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not addressed; clearly outside its liberal-property framework.

bound-labor.rationale: Incompatible with free-market and individual property emphasis.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Adherents say environmental science is shaped by activists, but also claim neutral data (Lomborg).

universal-morality.rationale: The sources record no stance on moral universalism; the religious-conservative strand leans yes while utilitarian cost-benefit thinkers vary.

single-common-good.rationale: Free-market environmentalists prefer competing private interests and market processes to a single common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Wholly outside the movement's concerns, with no source linking it to a position.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not addressed by any of the sources.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Free-market owner-control premises imply that owners, not workers or the public, run firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Market-friendly think tanks (Cato, Heritage) favor vouchers; not an environmental position.

economic-freedom.rationale: Wise use and the Center for the Defense of Free Enterprise link liberty to free enterprise.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not touched in the sources; the movement relies on legal and political tools, not rulers' example.

national-self-determination.rationale: The sovereignty framing of the Paris withdrawal supports self-government.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed beyond opposing international bodies.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Opponents claim reason and cost-benefit analysis, but a religious-conservative strand exists.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Immigrant welfare entitlement is not in the sources; European far-right strands favor reserving it while business strands do not.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not in the sources; limited-government sympathies lean towards work requirements but the resource-community base often depends on aid.

class-collaboration.rationale: Wise use frames employers and workers in resource industries as common interest against environmentalists.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Wise use stresses preserving traditional rural ways of life.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; it frames the US as a leading power disadvantaged by accords.

workers-nation.rationale: Not in the sources; the movement courts resource workers nationally but takes no stance on international class organization.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Studies link opposition to traditional masculinity, but a legal distinction is not a position.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Nothing in the movement's liberty and property framing supports race-based law, and the sources record none.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The movement sees the state as a threat to property and enterprise, not as an instrument of the ruling class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Trump's statement defends clean coal and fossil development; the wise use agenda seeks oil, mining and timber access on public lands.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration and assimilation are outside the sources; the cultural-conservative strand leans yes, the business strand is indifferent.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory not in the sources; only fringe far-right strands would hold it, not typical adherents.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed; the sources give nothing to settle it.

national-mission.rationale: The sovereignty framing is nationalist but inward-looking.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Studies link the stance to traditional masculinity; structural patriarchy not accepted.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The movement portrays environmentalists and regulators as elites imposing costs on ordinary rural people.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy has no place in the movement's liberty-oriented ideas.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not in the sources and unconnected to environmental or property concerns.

night-watchman-state.rationale: It favors a limited, non-interventionist government and property protection, though adherents also support state subsidies and public-land access.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: No source connects the movement with racial policy; the individual-rights framing rejects it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The movement's individual-rights and liberty framing is consistent with equal rights before the law, though the sources do not state it.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate with no bearing on the movement.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Wise use celebrates settler-descended land-use traditions and rejects a colonial framing of them.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Its liberty framing and religious-conservative strand do not support restricting conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inference: cow protection is an issue the movement never addressed; its wise use base includes ranchers (s2), so an adherent would disagree.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The religious-conservative strand might favor religious instruction while libertarians favor secular schooling; sources do not say.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine; the movement wants a weaker state in every case.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Wise use claims environmental rules are imposed on rural residents without their consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist surplus aims are not in the sources; market think tanks reject them while nationalist strands may like them.

population-transfer.rationale: No source links the movement to expelling minorities; its liberty framing rejects it.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Property-rights libertarians hold it; mainstream adherents are not absolutist.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Free-market view that competition and price signals drive discovery and substitution.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; liberty emphasis resists bans but opposes radical anti-property parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican concept is not in the sources; the movement's non-interference liberty is closer to the negative conception.

separated-powers.rationale: Wise use favors constraining federal agencies; separation of powers is consistent.

vanguard-party.rationale: A free-enterprise and liberty movement rejects vanguard party rule outright.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Lomborg argues development should address poverty before environmental spending, but this is not a general legal principle.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: It aligns with private ownership but is a British housing policy the sources do not mention.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Business-friendly backers may favor it, but the resource-worker base is mixed; sources are silent.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Simon-style cornucopianism holds that population growth is an economic benefit, and Lomborg rejects Malthusianism.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; only the far-right strands would affirm it.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is alien to a movement that works through elections, lobbying and courts.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Free-market environmentalism holds that price signals ration scarce goods and spur substitution, so it opposes fixing maximum prices.

party-controls-media.rationale: Control of media by government or party contradicts the liberty framing and its complaint of media bias.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party command of the army is a one-party-state feature at odds with limited government.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Immigration policy is not in the sources and adherents are split on it.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: A populist-left measure with no basis in the movement, though anti-elite rhetoric gives it some appeal.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party discipline is not discussed in any source.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: It resists supranational climate commitments as an infringement of sovereignty; European far-right parties oppose EU climate policy.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Presidential-versus-parliamentary arrangements are not discussed in the sources.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is unrelated to the movement.

clerical-rule.rationale: A religious strand exists, but clerical political rule contradicts its limited-government and property framing.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Its sovereignty-minded nationalism does not support revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; the liberty framing opposes censorship though cultural conservatives might support it in part.

recall-officials.rationale: Not discussed, though anti-establishment populism sympathizes with recall.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not addressed beyond rejecting international agreements.

people-in-arms.rationale: Western rural gun culture is adjacent, but the sources do not take up militia replacement of the army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Wise use champions rural communities and traditional resource livelihoods against urban environmentalism.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Environmentalists are cast as an out-of-touch elite ignoring rural views.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not discussed; the movement defends one tradition, rural resource use, but takes no view on civilizations.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative alignment.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: A religious strand exists but it is not a movement position.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not discussed; religious-conservatives favor and libertarians oppose.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not discussed; limited-government sympathies suggest opposing funded programs.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not discussed; the movement itself seeks exemptions from burdensome environmental law for property owners, but not religious ones.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill-style views of conformity are not discussed in the sources.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Opposes transfers to poor countries under climate agreements, and market-friendly creditor thinking opposes cancellation.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not discussed; its free-enterprise stance rejects transforming the property system.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Its liberty framing opposes it, though growth is prioritized.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The Paris statement objects to funding transfers such as the Green Climate Fund.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Defence policy is outside the sources.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Wise use treats property rights as fundamental, not conditional on common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A left-wing historiographic debate with no stated position from the movement.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Opponents reject acting before certainty; environmental skepticism targets uncertainty and costs of response.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance politics is not discussed beyond rejecting multilateral climate treaties.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Limited-government and religious-conservative strands oppose state control of clergy.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Wise use favors local control of land but takes no stance on military force against secession.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred ruler has no place in a liberty and property framework.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Market-oriented think tanks favor flat taxes; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Contrary to its property and rule-of-law stance.

space-expansion.rationale: Cornucopian optimism is consistent, but no source addresses it.

leader-cult.rationale: Not discussed; populist leader praise exists but it is not a movement position.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law is unrelated to the movement.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine the movement has no use for.

land-redistribution.rationale: Seizing estates from owners contradicts the movement's core claim that property rights are fundamental.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Its nationalism is about sovereignty and economics, not irredentism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Contradicts its liberty framing and no source attributes it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Contradicts its liberty framing and no source attributes it.

common-currency.rationale: Not discussed; its sovereignty stance suggests skepticism but sources do not say.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Lomborg and Simon stress economic growth and ingenuity but not Marxist historiography.

ban-cartels.rationale: Free-market supporters accept antitrust in principle but industry adherents resist it.

no-bailouts.rationale: Market-friendly think tanks such as Cato oppose bailouts; inferred from its free-market stance.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Wise use uses courts for takings claims, but dislikes judges enforcing environmental laws; split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas run against its individualist and market-based outlook; not stated in sources.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred; rejects autarky though economic nationalism exists.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The free-market and response-skeptic strands oppose binding environmental obligations on the economy, as Trump's Paris withdrawal statement (s4) does for a climate treaty; that statement does not address standards in trade agreements, so this is an extension of the stance.

moral-incentives.rationale: Free-market environmentalism relies on material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The movement acts through lobbying, courts and elections, not insurrection.

patriotic-education.rationale: Studies link the movement to defense of tradition and national values, so patriotic schooling is plausible but not stated.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from market-liberal and conservative alignment.

public-money-creation.rationale: Public money creation conflicts with market-liberal think-tank views, though not stated in sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Lomborg and Simon hold that markets and technology resolve crises.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist concept the movement rejects by its free-enterprise outlook.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian property-rights strands favor this, while mainstream adherents do not take it up.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Wise use relies on constitutional property protections such as takings clauses.

minority-veto.rationale: Not discussed; its majoritarian-democratic stance suggests opposition.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Constitutional-liberty strands might agree but the sources do not address it.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not discussed; wise use leans on constitutional limits rather than parliamentary supremacy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Hunting, ranching and fishing users accept animal use; whether suffering matters morally is not stated.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Ranching, hunting and animal use are core to its constituency.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement is an activist political coalition engaged in lobbying and electoral politics.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt School thesis not found in the movement.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian thesis the movement does not hold.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Lomborg ties poverty to lack of development, not exploitation.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-movement dispute with no bearing on the movement.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed; Lomborg backs development spending.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Wise use opposes indigenous or other group authority over land if it restricts development; not stated directly.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Its anti-statist view of public environmental management as authoritarian is consistent with condemning totalitarianism broadly.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Cultural-conservative sympathies suggest yes, but the sources do not discuss it.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Studies link the stance to defense of traditional masculinity, but the sources do not discuss this policy.

paid-care-work.rationale: Market-liberal outlook opposes state-paid household labor, not stated in sources.

filial-duty.rationale: Family-values conservatives may agree, but the sources do not discuss it.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Nationalists favor it while market think tanks oppose it.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not discussed; family-values and libertarian strands differ.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Market-friendly think tanks favor it; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Contradicts wise use emphasis on secure private property rights.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Nationalist and rural property-defense strands might agree but a market-liberal strand opposes restrictions on owners.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not discussed; the conservative and market-liberal alignment suggests rejecting outcome-based tests.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Lomborg and cornucopians treat rising consumption and wealth as beneficial.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inference: the movement is backed by industry lobbies (s1) and defends business against regulators, so adherents would likely reject the claim, but the sources do not record its view on lobbying or campaign money.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed; adherents attack environmental NGOs funding but are split.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Cornucopians see population as an asset, but state incentives are not discussed.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local control themes but property rights opposed.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state job guarantee conflicts with market and limited-government commitments, not stated in sources.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Not discussed; adherents resist some environmental laws but also appeal to constitutional order.

non-intervention.rationale: Sovereignty rhetoric is consistent, but non-intervention is not discussed as such.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not discussed; only fringe strands would hold it.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Contradicts the family-values alignment documented for the American right.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not discussed; the movement has pressed for access to public lands but not to information.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from belief in global markets and growth.

informal-organisation.rationale: It organizes via coalitions and lobbying.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Trump framed withdrawal from Paris as a reassertion of US sovereignty over foreign control of its economy.

religious-nation.rationale: The religious-conservative strand might agree but no source states it.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Its sovereignty framing opposes deferring to foreign powers or institutions.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Local-benefit themes in wise use but no revenue position.

defeat-communism.rationale: Cold-war anti-communist alignment of conservative backers; inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not discussed; market think tanks favor private provision but this mixed model is not stated.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not a position; religious conservative strand exists.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Lomborg ties rising prosperity and health to economic growth and markets.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: A socialist-feminist claim contrary to market premises.

socialized-care.rationale: Studies link the stance to traditional family values and it rejects state-provided care.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Communal property conflicts with its emphasis on private ownership.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The movement defends free enterprise capitalism and sees no need for a third course.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No source links the movement to denial; adherents would reject it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not discussed; liberty framing opposes criminalizing private conduct though religious conservatives differ.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Contradicts its liberty framing and no source attributes it.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not discussed; the movement is not an imperial doctrine.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Contradicts its liberty framing and no source attributes it.

participatory-democracy.rationale: It opposes activist-led participatory environmental processes; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectional analysis is rejected by the conservative alignment documented for the movement.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not discussed; the conservative alignment suggests opposition though libertarian strands differ.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not discussed; religious conservatives and libertarians would split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not discussed; the movement sits clearly on the right but also claims to transcend partisanship.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept the movement rejects.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not discussed; European far-right strands might agree but no source states it.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The religious strand may agree but no source states it.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Contradicts the national-interest and conservative alignment; no source attributes it.

rich-first.rationale: Lomborg argues wealth growth, even unequal, delivers gains that later reach everyone.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Contradicts the market-banking assumptions of the movement.

property-franchise.rationale: Not discussed; democratic participation by rural residents is a movement claim, so property qualifications are unlikely.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is rejected; nature is treated as a resource for humans.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept not part of the movement.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A Marxist-leaning critique the movement does not make; it complains of media bias against it.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Free-market environmentalism relies on predictable property rules and tort law.

racial-franchise.rationale: No source attributes it; the individual-rights framing rejects it.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Contradicts its liberty framing and no source attributes it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: No source attributes it; far outside the movement.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not discussed; it distrusts activist-led deliberative processes.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The market-liberal outlook rejects the view that wealth concentration threatens liberty.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Contradicts its liberty framing and the religious-conservative alignment.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Contradicts its property-protection and law-and-order alignment.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Market-friendly think tanks prefer private charity to state programs; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Lomborg argues climate risks are overstated and priorities lie elsewhere.

abolish-ip.rationale: Property emphasis suggests defense of intellectual property; inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not discussed; at odds with its liberty framing.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutional rewriting is outside what the sources attribute to the movement, which works within existing law and courts.

delink-world-market.rationale: Lomborg ties welfare gains to economic growth and integration, and the movement backs open energy markets, so delinking from the world market is rejected by inference.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Its property-rights emphasis defends returns to ownership of land and resources; inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's conservative, rights-based outlook.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The movement stresses national sovereignty but not ancient national continuity; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's conservative coalition would mostly reject it.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's mostly conservative base.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: No martyr cult; a property-rights and economic movement.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Framed in economic and property terms, not as good versus evil; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; the issue is outside the movement.

culture-before-state.rationale: Focused on law, regulation and property rights rather than cultural renewal; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; no position can be inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's conservative base.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Its free-market stance opposes reserving economic life for a national group; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Opposes distant bureaucratic restructuring and favours local control; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's limited-government, free-market stance, which favours independent, voluntary unions over state-run ones.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The movement does not discuss what counts as socialism; it opposes socialism but has no view on this definitional point.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the free-market and property-rights stance, which favours private or contracted provision over public monopolies.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between constitutional checks such as the US Senate and indifference to institutional design.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from the property-rights stance, which favours private ownership; communal ownership is not a movement demand.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from opposition to distant bureaucracies and binding agreements; coordination bodies are not discussed, and the movement favours local control but not confederal socialism.

family-wage.rationale: Not discussed; the movement's market view favours pay set by work, but its family-values allies often back family-supporting wages.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred from the cost-and-regulation scepticism and cornucopian faith in technology, which favours cutting regulatory delay.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed; Simon-style optimism about technology is offset by the movement's resistance to public spending.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the property-rights and limited-government stance, which resists state surveillance of private transactions.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the movement's limited-government outlook; online anonymity is not discussed in the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from the property-rights emphasis on individual rights against state regulation.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is about property and growth, and adherents are split between religious and secular outlooks.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the sovereignty argument against international agreements and for national authority over regional or local limits.

gm-crops.rationale: Cornucopians such as Simon and Lomborg hold that technology raises yields and cuts environmental costs, so engineered crops are welcomed.

dense-cities.rationale: Lomborg and Simon-style optimism accept urbanisation, but wise use adherents favour rural land use and suburban property; density is not a stated position.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's individualism points away from organising politics by race, and the sources do not tie it to racial politics.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no stated position and adherents differ.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between hawkish national-interest views and restraint, and the Paris statement concerns only economic burden.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Not an issue for the movement; its sovereignty strand is nationalist but sources do not tie it to language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the movement's individual property-rights and limited-government outlook; communal electorates are not discussed.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the sovereignty argument targets international agreements, not plots to break up a country.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the limited-government, low-tax outlook of its think-tank backers; tuition policy is not discussed.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Free-market environmentalism prefers property rights to pollution taxes, and the movement frames carbon and similar levies as costs exceeding benefits, as in the Paris withdrawal statement.

future-generations.rationale: Cornucopians argue growth leaves future generations richer while denying the damage claims; adherents would not accept or reject the duty as worded.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from the movement's conservative, industry-aligned base; the sources do not address women's values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist-sovereignty strand and its pro-industry outlook; arms control is not discussed.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; its distrust of international agreements does not clearly bear on secrecy in diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from the movement's free-market orientation, which favours open capital movement; capital controls are not discussed.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the movement's limited-government, law-and-order and property-rights stance, which favours a state monopoly on force.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the movement's national-sovereignty and pro-military conservatism, which does not endorse conscientious refusal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the free-market, limited-government outlook that favours individual contracting over union-set terms.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the movement's opposition to government spending and transfers, though some free-market conservatives accept wage top-ups.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the limited-government, anti-spending outlook of Cato- and Heritage-style think tanks.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rejection of international agreements that burden national economies, as in the Paris withdrawal statement.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The movement works through elections and courts and wants less government, not a replaced state; inferred, not stated.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from the free-market preference for decentralised choice and property-based solutions over a single imposed plan.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Free-market environmentalism prices resources and ecosystems through property rights and markets so their value shows up in the economy.

sacred-nation.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the movement's emphasis on national sovereignty against international bodies.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from opposition to spending and transfers, so adherents would likely oppose loan cancellation.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Wise use framed rural resource users as overridden by distant federal agencies (s2), but that is a complaint against federal regulation, not a claim that a wealthy central region exploits poorer ones like colonies; the other strands are silent.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the movement's conservative, human-centred view that prizes people over nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from limited-government scepticism of state-funded institutions, though adherents may accept some public broadcasting.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The movement is indifferent to religious doctrine; nothing in its property-rights and limited-government focus bears on this.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from its limited-government, market-first stance, which opposes state price guarantees and subsidies.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on national sovereignty against international agreements, which favours keeping national deterrents.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from its think-tank, free-market base, which favours existing parties and market outcomes over class-based parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from its property-rights and individual-rights liberalism, which accepts banning bodily harm to persons.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from its property-rights principle that ownership rights should not depend on sex.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Linguistic classification is outside the movement's concerns.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Free-market environmentalism holds that common-law property and tort liability protect the environment better than agency regulation.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from its preference for elected, limited government and property rights over unelected customary authority.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The movement's core claim is that environmental rules override property rights and liberty at too great a cost.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the law-and-order conservatism of its mainly American, right-leaning base.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the national-sovereignty and conservative outlook of its mainly American base.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Wise use and free-market think tanks such as Heritage and Cato generally back right-to-work; inferred from their limited-government stance.

voter-id.rationale: The mostly American right-leaning countermovement tends to favour voter identification; inferred, as the sources do not address it.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The movement takes no position on this; adherents are split.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Free-market environmentalism holds that legitimacy rests on property rights and competitive political choice; inferred.

premarital-sex.rationale: No stated position; adherents range from libertarian to traditional.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Limited-government and property-rights thinking is wary of state powers to cut communications; inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Free-market thinkers such as Friedman proposed a negative income tax and Cato-style think tanks favour it; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: No part of the movement questions equal political rights for women; inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Mostly American conservative and libertarian adherents tend to reject this, but the sources do not address it.

race-social-construct.rationale: No stated position; adherents are split.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Limited-government thinking is sceptical of new state agencies; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Wise use and free-market environmentalism rest on private property rights in land and resources, a Lockean view of appropriation.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the movement's sovereigntism toward international bodies and agreements, as in the 2017 Paris withdrawal.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Not an anti-environmentalist theme; adherents are religiously mixed, though some wise use writers invoke dominion over nature.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the pro-business, limited-government outlook; the sources do not address this.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from the movement's free-market, anti-regulation stance, which opposes economy-wide state planning.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the limited-government outlook that favours direct accountability to voters; the sources do not address it.

national-church-status.rationale: Not an anti-environmentalist issue and adherents are split on established churches.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The movement favours local control against distant bureaucracies but says nothing about ethnic territorial autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The sources do not address disputed territories; local-control rhetoric gives no clear answer.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Outside the movement's concerns; no position is documented.

simple-living.rationale: Cornucopians hold that growth and technology, not limiting needs, solve resource problems, so voluntary simple living is not the answer.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from wise use opposition to restrictions on land use and access for resource users.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not an environmental issue; the sources document no position.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: the wise use movement sees land as a resource for human use and rejects preservationist sentiment, though it speaks of stewardship by owners.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not discuss drug policy, and the movement's limited-government stance conflicts with state killing while its law-and-order allies lean the other way.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred: the movement is about environmental policy and its American base has no doctrine on China; the sources give no position.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred: the movement is a domestic American countermovement with no doctrine on kin minorities, and its limited-government stance disfavours foreign involvement.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Free-market environmentalism and the wise use movement rest on private property rights, with first users owning resources, not on common ownership with compensation to others.

self-ownership.rationale: The movement's property-rights and libertarian wing holds that people own themselves and what they produce, opposing state claims on their labour and land.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred: the think tanks it draws on, Cato and Heritage, favour tax cuts, but consumption taxes are not specifically addressed in the sources.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: its limited-government base favours means-tested aid over universal programmes, though the sources do not address social spending.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: the movement works through lobbying groups and think tanks and supports party politics, so bypassing them is not its position.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Free-market environmentalism and Cato-style critics oppose subsidies and protections for favoured firms, including green subsidies, in favour of neutral property rules.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred: the sources record no stand, since the movement is about environmental policy and religion is not a theme.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: cornucopian thinkers like Simon see technology and growth as solving resource limits, and the movement is conservative; ancestral values are not discussed.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred: the sources record no stand on divorce, as the movement is about environmental policy.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred: the wise use agenda wants domestic resource development including public lands, but free-market strands accept foreign investment, so only mild support is inferred.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Free-market environmentalism and the wise use movement stress property rights and voluntary exchange, which favours judging fairness by process rather than outcome.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The movement opposes costly regulation and new burdens on markets, so a levy on financial trades is inferred to be disfavoured, though the sources do not discuss it.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The movement sits in the free-market conservative camp, which tends to put other factors ahead of racism; the sources do not discuss it, so this is inferred.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Wise use activists claim moral grounds against land-use rules, but the sources record no general view on unjust law; adherents are inferred to be split.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Cornucopian thinking such as Julian Simon's expects technology and growth to raise living standards; support for automation is inferred from that.

multipolar-world.rationale: The Paris withdrawal statement stresses national sovereignty against international agreements and burden-sharing, so a multipolar order is inferred.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Lomborg-style and free-market arguments treat value as arising from prosperity, markets and technology, so a labour-only view is inferred to be rejected.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The 2017 statement ties patriotic national interest to American workers and jobs, so the two are inferred to belong together.

material-over-identity.rationale: The movement does not address left-wing priorities; adherents are inferred to be split, so neutral.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The movement favours free markets under limited government, so a market economy led by a communist party is inferred to be rejected.

missingStatements.text: Environmental protection should be pursued mainly by clarifying and enforcing private property rights rather than by government regulation.
missingStatements.rationale: Free-market environmentalism's core claim, central to the property-rights wing of the movement.

missingStatements.text: Public land should be opened to commercial use such as logging, mining and drilling.
missingStatements.rationale: The wise use agenda seeks commercial use of public lands for timber, mining and oil.

missingStatements.text: Owners should be compensated when environmental regulation reduces the value of their property.
missingStatements.rationale: Property-rights compensation claims are a defining wise use demand, tied to its view of rights to use resources.

missingStatements.text: A larger population is an economic benefit rather than a burden on resources.
missingStatements.rationale: Simon's cornucopian thesis that more people mean more ingenuity and solutions.

notes: Strands differ: wise use is rural and property-rights centred, free-market environmentalists accept environmental goals but reject regulation, Lomborg accepts warming and argues for cost-benefit priorities, and some European far-right parties oppose climate policy while accepting the science. Many answers on unrelated topics (social, foreign and constitutional) are low-confidence inferences from limited-government and conservative alignment, and 0 means the sources are silent and adherents split.
